intro: Que, donde and quien join a noun with more information: el libro que compré, la ciudad donde vivo.
p.que.consejo: It joins a noun with more information: «el libro que compré». No accent; with an accent, «qué», it is a question.
p.donde.consejo: It speaks of a place and already includes «en»: «la ciudad donde vivo». No accent; with an accent it is a question.
p.quien.consejo: It refers to a person, mainly after a preposition: «la amiga con quien vivo».
p.quienes.consejo: It is the plural of «quien»: «las amigas con quienes vivo». No accent.
p.compré.consejo: It is the past of «comprar» with yo. The accent marks the stress at the end: kom-PRÉ.
p.vivo.consejo: From «vivir»: to have your home in a place. The v sounds like b: BI-bo. It is also «alive»: un animal vivo.
p.la ciudad.consejo: It is feminine and ends in -d: «la ciudad», «las ciudades». The «ci» sounds «thyu».
p.la amiga.consejo: It is feminine: «la amiga». For a boy: «el amigo». For a mixed group: «los amigos».
p.el libro.consejo: It is masculine and ends in -o: «el libro». Plural: «los libros».
p.la plaza.consejo: It is read PLA-tha in Spain. It is usually the centre of village life: «la plaza del pueblo».
p.pequeña.consejo: It is feminine; the masculine is «pequeño». The «ñ» sounds like «ny»: pe-KE-nya.
p.nuevo.consejo: It changes with the noun: nuevo, nueva, nuevos, nuevas. The v sounds like b: NWE-bo.
p.el vecino.consejo: It is who lives near you. «La vecina» is the woman. The «ci» sounds «thi».
b1.texto:
To join a noun with more information, use **que**, **donde** or **quien**. None of them takes an accent.

- **que** works for things and people: el libro **que** compré; la amiga **que** vive aquí.
- **donde** speaks of a place and already includes «en»: la ciudad **donde** vivo (= la ciudad en la que vivo).
- **quien / quienes** speaks of people, mainly after a preposition: la amiga con **quien** vivo; las amigas con **quienes** vivo.

Put the information **right after** the noun it explains.
b2.f0.texto: The city where I live is small.
b2.f1.texto: The book that I bought is new.
b2.f2.texto: The friend I live with is called Ana.
b2.f3.texto: The café that is in the square is good.
b2.f4.texto: The square where we meet has a fountain.
b2.f5.texto: The neighbours who live there are friendly.
b2.f6.texto: The friends I go out with live nearby.
b2.f7.texto: The book I am looking for is about this city.
b4.texto:
Three forms, three uses:

- **que** → thing or person: el pan **que** compro; la chica **que** vive aquí.
- **donde** → place: el café **donde** trabajo = el café **en el que** trabajo.
- **con quien, de quien, a quien…** → person, after a preposition: la chica **con quien** hablo. Plural: **quienes**.

The information goes between the noun and the rest of the sentence: **el libro que compré** es nuevo.
b4.e0.texto: The bread that I buy smells very good.
b4.e1.texto: The café where I work opens early.
b4.e2.texto: The girl I talk to is my neighbour.
b5.f0.texto: The city where I live has streets that smell of bread in the morning.
b5.f1.texto: In the centre there is a square where the children play.
b5.f2.texto: The houses that surround the square have balconies full of flowers.
b5.f3.texto: A fountain that sings day and night wakes the birds.
b5.f4.texto: My favourite street goes down to the river that cuts through the city.
b5.f5.texto: In the neighbourhood where I grew up, the baker knew all the neighbours.
b5.f6.texto: The children who ran along the street shouted her name.
b5.f7.texto: Today I go back with the friends I used to play with then.
b5.f8.texto: We go together into the bakery where it always smells of warm bread.
b5.f9.texto: The baker gives us a piece of bread that is still burning hot.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Donde» speaks of a place and already includes «en».
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Quien» is for people, not for cities.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Cual» needs an article: la cual. Here there is none.
b6.pregunta: Which word goes with a place?
b7.o0: El libro donde compré es nuevo.
b7.o0.refuerzo: «Donde» is for places. A book is not a place.
b7.o1: El libro que compré es nuevo.
b7.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «Que» joins the noun with what you did.
b7.o2: El libro quien compré es nuevo.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «Quien» is for people, not for books.
b7.pregunta: «Compré un libro. El libro es nuevo.» How are they joined?
b8.frase: El libro que compré es nuevo
b8.traduccion: The book that I bought is new
b9.o1.refuerzo: «Lo» does not join a noun with more information.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Well done! After a preposition, a person takes «quien».
b9.pregunta: Which word goes with a person after «con»?
b10.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «The book that I bought is new.»
b11.o0.refuerzo: Correct! Since it is not a question, «donde» has no accent.
b11.o1.refuerzo: «Dónde» with an accent is for asking: ¿dónde vives?
b11.o2.refuerzo: For a place you use «donde», with no accent.
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Quien» is singular. Here there are several people.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes! Plural with plural: las amigas con quienes.
b12.o2.refuerzo: «Donde» is for places, not for people.
p.vemos.consejo: From «ver». The v sounds like b in Spain.
p.balcones.consejo: Plural of «balcón». The stress is on KO.
p.favorita.consejo: The v sounds like b. The stress is on RI.
p.corrían.consejo: From «correr», to run. The -ían ending is the past form.
p.gritaban.consejo: From «gritar», to shout. The -aban ending is the past form.
p.jugaba.consejo: The j sounds like h. The -aba ending is for repeated past actions.
p.entramos.consejo: From «entrar», to go in. The -amos ending means «we».
p.quema.consejo: From «quemar», to burn. The qu sounds like «k».
